entities.name: HIV-1 Vif
observations: HIV-1 virion infectivity factor; supplied sequence is 193 aa and matches reviewed HIV-1 Vif references at 85.5% identity over 100% of query and target coverage (E-value 5.35e-123).
Vif recruits a host CUL5-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase complex with elongin B/C and CBFB, promoting APOBEC3F and APOBEC3G polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation.
Vif can also inhibit APOBEC3G cytidine-deaminase activity independently of degradation and may inhibit APOBEC3G mRNA translation.
Annotated as a host-cytoplasmic, peripheral-membrane, and virion-associated protein; it can bind RNA and metal ions.
Sequence-derived properties: 193 aa, approximately 22.4 kDa, theoretical pI 9.87, predicted charge at pH 7 approximately +13.8.
The complete sequence matches Pfam Vif (PF00559.24), positions 1-193, i-Evalue 2.2e-104.

entities.name: APOBEC3F
observations: Host antiviral cytidine deaminase targeted by HIV-1 Vif for ubiquitination and degradation.

entities.name: APOBEC3G
observations: Host antiviral cytidine deaminase targeted and inhibited by HIV-1 Vif through degradation and additional proteasome-independent mechanisms.

entities.name: CUL5 E3 ligase complex
observations: HIV-1 Vif hijacks this host ubiquitin-ligase machinery, together with elongin B/C and CBFB, to target APOBEC3F and APOBEC3G.

entities.name: HIV-1 Vif host restriction antagonism
observations: The protein is a viral immune-evasion factor whose main cellular role is neutralizing APOBEC3-mediated restriction, thereby supporting HIV replication and infectious virion production.
